opening: I'm applying for the {role} role at {company}. I'm a software engineer at Sky9 IT Craft in Rajkot, where I build and ship .NET and Angular products for clients in aviation, mailing, and waste management.
body: What I bring is end to end ownership. I designed and built ArenaHub, a sports venue booking platform, from the database up: an ASP.NET Core Minimal API, an Angular frontend, PostgreSQL on Neon, Razorpay payments, map-based discovery with Leaflet, and file uploads to Cloudflare R2. On client work I've shipped multi-factor authentication and GoCardless payments for an aircraft management platform, RDLC-based invoicing and reconciliation for a US mailing service, and multi-tenant admin dashboards with Azure storage for a UK waste management company. I also work with AI coding agents daily, but review and hold every line to the same standard I would write myself.
whyThem: [Why-this-company paragraph here. One researched detail about their product, stack, market, or engineering blog, connected to your work.]
closing: I'd welcome the chance to talk about how I can help {company} ship work like this, and I'm available for a conversation at your convenience. Thank you for your time and consideration.
swapNotes:
Per application, change exactly these three things, then run: node build-cover-letter.js
1. recipient.company  (appears in the recipient block, the greeting, and every {company} token)
2. role  (appears in the opening line via {role})
3. whyThem  (replace the placeholder with one researched detail: their product, stack, market, or a blog post, connected to your work)
If you find the hiring manager's name, set recipient.name to it and the greeting becomes 'Dear {name},'. Otherwise leave 'Hiring Manager' and the greeting reads 'Dear {company} Hiring Team,'.
date stays 'auto' and always prints the day you build.
Before sending, rename the tailored PDF: Harshit_Talshania_Cover_Letter_[Company].pdf
